confirmed.proposal: Exactly the Dev ruling: hot-path fallible functions return a 4-byte [[nodiscard]] enum-class status (0 = ok, value in EAX, test = test eax,eax). Details move out-of-band into a pending_error struct {error_code ec; string_view msg; uint64 sym1, sym2} that is a MEMBER of the backend instance (vm_backend / interpreter — no statics, per-engine, parallel_for workers each own a backend), written by ONE cold __declspec(noinline) raise(...) helper that returns the failure status. Error text stays byte-identical by construction: same {ec,msg,syms} through the same format_error, both backends share the machinery.
confirmed.impact: ~122k op dispatches/tick x ~1.5-3 result layers, each saving ~7 stores + 1 stack reload + frame/register pressure: ballpark 1.5-2.5M cycles/tick = 0.4-0.6 ms of the 6.8 ms GLOOM tick (4-8%), plus un-estimated secondary wins from run_dispatch register allocation (probe frame halved). confirmed.problem: checked_result<void> is {std::error_code(16B) + string_view(16B) + 2x uint64 symbol ids} = 48 bytes. Cross-boundary APIs (environment::get etc.) keep full checked_result; only exec_* signatures and VM_TRY_OP/VM_TRY_OP_SHARED change. Error text stays byte-identical (details are moved, not changed).

confirmed.title: Dispatch loop pays 3 invariant member-tests per iteration: ip-bounds (dead given halt-terminated chunks), debug_hook_, and a bottom is_unwinding_ check even for ops that cannot unwind
confirmed.problem: Per dispatched op the loop head reloads f.code->code (data+size), tests f.ip >= code.size(), and tests debug_hook_; the loop bottom tests is_unwinding_ before ++f.ip. But (a) every chunk the compiler produces is halt-terminated (program 432, function bodies 482, param-default chunks 472), so the head bounds test duplicates op_halt's exit for well-formed code; (b) pure ops (op_const, op_load, op_pop, op_dup, op_null/true/false, op_jump, op_decl_var scalar path) can never set is_unwinding_ yet fall through the bottom check; (c) debug_hook_ is loaded per statement forever even though no debugger is attached in production runs.
confirmed.proposal: (a) Prove/enforce 'ip only ever points at a real instruction' (audit fall_off_script_frame callers, yield/resume ips, handler_ip targets) and drop the head bounds test, letting op_halt be the sole frame exit; (b) end never-unwinding cases with `++f.ip; continue;` (or group them before a no-check tail label) so only user-code ops reach the unwind test; (c) fold debug_hook_ and any other rare whole-run modes into one 'slow mode' byte tested once, or swap in a separate instrumented dispatch loop when a debug session arms (the hook already re-arms deadline state at attach, 461-462).
confirmed.impact: Removes 2-3 loads+branches from EVERY dispatch iteration (~100-120k/tick). Even at 3-6 cycles saved per iteration that is 0.3-0.7M cycles/tick (~2-3%), and shrinking the shared loop head improves I-cache/branch-predictor behavior for all ops.

(b) requires per-case tail duplication (code size) but is semantics-free. (c) must keep the attach path able to interrupt a running loop — the existing debug_controller_ check inside execution_budget_exhausted (446) already covers the async case.

confirmed.title: Catch-variable check is a per-instruction runtime tax on the hottest ops; the binding is lexically resolvable at compile time
confirmed.problem: Every exec_load (vm_backend.cpp:2833) and every fused operand resolution (fused_ident_value, vm_backend.cpp:3948) compares the loaded symbol against backend-global current_catch_var_id_; worse, the fused compare/compound fast paths are gated on `current_catch_var_id_ == 0` (vm_backend.cpp:4274, 4343) so ALL fused fast paths shut off while any catch block is executing — including for unrelated variables. The interpreter twin pays the same compare per identifier (interpreter.cpp:2791) and disables its binary ident+ident fast path inside catch (2898), and re-interns the catch-var string on every caught exception (9913, try_stmt::catch_var is a raw std::string with no parse-stamped id — ast.hpp:572). The catch variable is a lexical binding: which loads refer to it is fully known at parse/compile time.
confirmed.proposal: Resolve the catch variable statically: intern catch_var once at parse (add catch_var_id to try_stmt), and have the vm_compiler mark the loads that lexically resolve to the catch variable (dedicated LOAD_EXCEPTION opcode or an ins.c flag), binding it like any scoped local. Then delete the current_catch_var_id_ compare from exec_load/fused_ident_value and drop it from the fused fast-path gates (interpreter: give the catch var a slot in the frame like other block locals). Keep a runtime assert during transition.
confirmed.impact: Removes a global-load+compare+branch from ~38k LOADs plus ~2 operand resolutions x (18k BINARY_FUSED + 10k FUSED_CMP_JUMP + 7.2k COMPOUND_FUSED) per GLOOM tick (~80-90k executions/tick), and un-gates every fused fast path inside catch bodies for all scripts (generality win: error-handling-heavy code currently runs de-optimized).
confirmed.risk: MEDIUM. The current dynamic check applies to ANY same-named symbol while a catch is active — including loads in functions CALLED from the catch block whose env-resolved globals share the name (frames don't scope current_catch_var_id_). confirmed.title: Fused binary ops re-classify their operator token every execution (is_numeric_binary_op 12-case switch) though the compiler fixed the op at fusion time
confirmed.problem: binary_fused_compute (18k/tick) runs `!has_custom_numeric_ops_ && is_numeric_binary_op(op)` per execution — the second half is a 12-case switch on a token that was baked into the fused proto at compile time and can never change; op_binary (9.4k/tick) does the same at 3925. Then the op-specific switch (4115/4137) re-dispatches the same token a second time. Related same-shape waste: env_lookup_cached re-checks/computes `cache.size() < code.size()*3` (two size loads + imul) on every cached lookup (1397-1400) when the cache could be sized once at chunk finalization.
confirmed.proposal: Stamp a `numeric_eligible` bit (from is_numeric_binary_op) into fused_binary_proto / the op_binary shape byte at compile time, so runtime is one bit-test plus the has_custom_numeric_ops_ load; optionally fold has_custom_numeric_ops_/catch-mode/debug into a single backend 'fast-mode' byte updated at its few mutation chokepoints so the whole gate is one compare. Pre-size env_lookup_cache when the chunk is finalized (code size is fixed then) and drop the per-lookup resize test.
confirmed.impact: ~27k BINARY(_FUSED) executions + 10k FUSED_CMP_JUMP per tick lose a switch-classification each (a few cycles), and every cached env lookup loses two loads+multiply. Modest alone (~0.1M cycles/tick) but shortens the hottest fast-path prologues where every branch counts for the predictor.
confirmed.risk: has_custom_numeric_ops_ CAN flip mid-run (operator registration from script), so only the token classification is precomputable — the runtime flag must stay a live load or the combined fast-mode byte must be updated at every registration/catch/debug transition (few, auditable chokepoints). Cache pre-sizing must handle chunks compiled before the cache-3x convention (single site in env_lookup_cached).
confirmed.verify_reason: CONFIRMED for binary_fused_compute: vm_backend.cpp:4110 runs `!has_custom_numeric_ops_ && is_numeric_binary_op(op)` per execution where p.op is baked at compile time (vm_compiler.cpp:1414) and never mutated afterward (all proto rewrites — fused_cmp_jump :265, fused_store :1505, fused_decl :1854 — are compile-time peepholes); callers are exec_binary_fused (:4071) + fused decl/store (:4202/:4237) = ~18.5k/tick. Also confirmed has_custom_numeric_ops_ flips mid-run (engine.cpp:2028, :2071-2075 add_overloaded_function of +-*/, :2146), so only the token classification is bakeable — the finding's risk note is accurate. REFUTED components: (1) op_binary at :3925 never runs the switch — the ONLY emit of op_binary is vm_compiler.cpp:1424 with binary_shape_none hardcoded (all shaped binaries become op_binary_fused at :1411-1418), so `ins.b != binary_shape_none` short-circuits false on every one of the 9.4k unfused BINARYs; same for op_return_binary(:10185)/entry(:10217), which are rewritten from op_binary (:691-692) inheriting b=none. The shape branches AND binary_fast_shape (:2181-2350) are unreachable dead code the optimizer can't prove dead. (2) FUSED_CMP_JUMP (10k/tick) never calls is_numeric_binary_op — exec_fused_cmp_jump :4274 gates on `!has_custom_numeric_ops_ && current_catch_var_id_ == 0` and the compiler fuses exactly the six comparisons (:4289). So the honest count is ~18.5k switch runs/tick, not 37k — the ~0.1M cycles/tick estimate is ~2x high; the switch compiles to a range-check + mask test (~4-6 inst, predicted branch), so realistic saving is <0.02ms of a 6.8ms tick. env_lookup_cached size check CONFIRMED at :1397-1400 and pre-sizing is sound (code.size() fixed post-compile, no runtime code growth found, cache touched only after the :1394 env gate, single-threaded per backend), but GLOOM's hot operands resolve via frame slots (fused_ident_value :3952-3955 returns before the cache), shrinking that win further.
confirmed.notes: Implementation: (a) fused_binary_proto (chunk.hpp:110-114) has 3 padding bytes after uint8_t op (fused_operand is uint32-aligned) — a numeric_eligible flag byte is layout-free; stamp it at vm_compiler.cpp:1414 as is_numeric_binary_op(op) so the bit is the same predicate by construction (zero semantic risk, no interpreter change needed — interpreter has its own equivalent gate at interpreter.hpp:530, untouched). Proto-bit stamping shifts no code, so no jump-target hazards. (b) The BIGGER cleanup this verification surfaced: exec_binary/exec_return_binary/_entry shape branches (:3925-3934, :10185-10193, :10217-10227) and all of binary_fast_shape (:2181-2350, ~170 lines duplicating the fused switch rows) are dead post-fusion — deleting them is an i-cache/code-size win and removes a parity-twin maintenance trap (three copies of the int/float rows exist: binary_fast_shape, binary_fused_compute, exec_fused_cmp_jump; deletion leaves two). Verify with an assert-on-shape!=none canary run of the full suite before deleting. (c) Do NOT pre-size env_lookup_cache at compile time for all chunks — 72 bytes/instruction (3 × 24-byte entries) eagerly penalizes cold functions; hoist the resize to frame push (once per frame) instead of per lookup. (d) The 'fold catch/debug into a fast-mode byte' sub-idea needs a chokepoint audit: current_catch_var_id_ is consulted INSIDE fused_ident_value (:3948) for lookup semantics, not just gating — that check must stay per-operand; debugger attach mid-run (DAP) is another mutation chokepoint. invariants.md has no section on chunk immutability — if pre-sizing or proto-stamping lands, add the 'chunk code/protos are immutable after compile' invariant it silently relies on.

refuted.title: exec_binary's std::optional<checked_result<script_value>> is a triple-status 80-byte temp per unfused BINARY
refuted.reason: The optional<checked_result<script_value>> block at vm_backend.cpp:3925-3933 is statically dead: vm_compiler.cpp:1424 is the ONLY op_binary emission and hardcodes binary_shape_none (all fusable shapes divert to op_binary_fused at vm_compiler.cpp:1412-1419; op_return_binary is an in-place rewrite of that same op_binary at vm_compiler.cpp:691-693, inheriting shape_none). So the guard `ins.b != binary_shape_none` never passes, the 80-byte optional is never constructed (it is declared inside the guard block), and binary_fast_shape (vm_backend.cpp:2181) is dormant dead code — known_divergences.md:35 already calls it 'the VM's dormant binary_fast_shape twins'. The 9.4k/tick unfused BINARYs go straight to binary_general (vm_backend.cpp:3936), whose by-value checked_result<script_value> return is RVO'd with ONE discriminant, not the claimed triple-status round trip. The size math (72B checked_result, 80B optional, zero-filled status fields on success emplace — checked_result.hpp:59-84) is correct but describes an object that never exists at runtime. The fused path (18k/tick) already has the proposed sink-based dest-addressing (binary_fused_compute, vm_backend.cpp:4109+).
